_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), Series GHF2E, SET-1. 27 pages: idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions + Q1; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-26, Hindi on every odd index (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi (no English overflow); last page idx 26 English (Q39). Question numbers run 1-39 unbroken. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (ms pages 0-10, 31/2/1 only): a bare OR after Q24, 25, 27, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38, 39 = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. No void note anywhere in the scheme. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme page images; each was also re-derived and agrees. Decimal points on this paper are RAISED (Q3: 6{\cdot}1; Q31: 8{\cdot}0). Opener of series 31/2: nothing skipped.

questions._figure: ILLUSTRATIVE - two photographs, Figure ‘X’ (an attached earlobe) and Figure ‘Y’ (a free earlobe); the stem states which figure shows which trait. Page idx 16.
questions.stem:
The lowest part of the ear called earlobe, is closely attached to the side of the head in some of us (Figure ‘X’), and not in others, called free earlobe (Figure ‘Y’). Attached and free earlobes are two variants found in human populations. The gene for free earlobe is dominant over attached earlobes.

(a) A man with attached earlobes marries a woman having free earlobes. 50% of their children have free earlobes and 50% have attached earlobes. Explain the inheritance of this trait and write the trait combinations of the progeny.

(b) Write the gene combinations of the father and the mother in the above case.
